Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the run chase! The umpires and the Pakistan fielders are in place and out comes the Bangladeshi opening pair of Parvez Hossain Emon and Tanzid Hasan. It will be the debutant, Salman Mirza, who will get proceedings underway with the ball. Let's go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Right then, Nelson (111) is what Bangladesh need to keep their winning run going and take a 1-0 lead in this T20I series. The pitch is always tricky here, but there might be some dew in the second innings which will aid the batters. Pakistan are missing their bug guns with the ball but early wickets can be the key to turning this match into a real contest. Should be an exciting watch, so stay tuned as the chase is up next.

Bangladesh will be delighted with that effort and Litton Das will be pleased that his string of losing tosses was broken and he made the right decision. However, it wasn't all positive to begin with as they conceded plenty of boundaries and there was even a dropped catch of Fakhar Zaman by Taskin Ahmed. But Taskin answered back by dismissing Ayub and from there on, the hosts took full advantage of the mistakes made by the opposition batters. Mustafizur Rahman really stood out with his spell as he gave away just 6 runs in 4 overs and even picked up a couple of wickets and Taskin finished things up with a three-wicket haul to bowl out Pakistan in the final over.

Pakistan had a completely changed look from the team that beat Bangladesh 3-0 just over a month or so ago and they had a clear approach with the bat, which was to go hard in the Powerplay. It did work for a couple of overs and Fakhar Zaman looked in devastating form but once that first wicket of Saim Ayub fell, reality hit them hard. The batters simply went after the bowlers and threw away their wickets with Zaman stranded at one end. He tried to steady the ship before again going hard at the bowlers but was sold down the river by Khushdil Shah, resulting in a run out. Abbas Afridi did muscle a few sixes but eventually, Pakistan kept losing wickets and mustered up just 110 runs.

Well then, a month of firsts continues for Bangladesh as they bowl out Pakistan for the first time ever in the T20I format after just having defeated Sri Lanka 2-1 in a bilateral T20I series not long ago. A wonderful bowling performance which was more often than not, backed up by the fielders and the hosts have restricted a new-look Pakistan side for an under-par score here.

Commentary.Commentary: DRINKS BREAK! Wow, what an entertaining first 10 overs. It all started with a flurry of boundaries but then came a flurry of wickets and just when it seemed to be settling down, Fakhar Zaman has again shown aggression in the previous over. Pakistan came firing out of the blocks but once the first wicket fell, the batters that came in simply couldn't get going. All four of Bangladesh's bowlers used so far, picked up a wicket each and there was even a run out that has got the hosts into the driving seat. However, Pakistan are playing a lot of all-rounders and there's Faheem Ashraf still to come, giving them hopes of achieving a par score.

Commentary.Commentary: Done and dusted with the pre-match formalities and it is now time to get the play underway. The umpires are out in the middle and so are the players of Bangladesh. It will be the duo of Fakhar Zaman and Saim Ayub to open the innings for Pakistan. Mahedi Hasan, the off-spinner to take the new ball. Let's play...

We are just a few minutes away from the start of the match, but first, the two sets of players and the mascots will lineup for the national anthems. It will be the national anthem of Pakistan followed by the national anthem of Bangladesh.

PITCH REPORT - Former Pakistani opener, Aamer Sohail, with the pitch report. He says that there has been rain around here in Dhaka, building up to the game. He mentions that the pitch sounds hard (as he knocks his hand on the wicket). He adds that there will be some moisture in the wicket and that will aid the spinners as well as pace off deliveries of pacers. He feels that the batters should look to get used to the pace of the wicket before playing their shots.

Pakistan (Playing XI) - Fakhar Zaman, Saim Ayub, Mohammad Haris (WK), Salman Agha (C), Hasan Nawaz, Mohammad Nawaz, Khushdil Shah, Faheem Ashraf, Abbas Afridi, Salman Mirza (On T20I debut), Abrar Ahmed.

Bangladesh (Playing XI) - Litton Das (C/WK), Tanzid Hasan, Parvez Hossain Emon, Tawhid Hridoy, Jaker Ali, Shamim Hossain, Mahedi Hasan, Rishad Hossain, Taskin Ahmed, Mustafizur Rahman, Tanzim Hasan Sakib.
TOSS - Bangladesh have won the toss and they will BOWL first.

All eyes will be on how Bangladesh's newfound confidence, particularly their in-form batting unit and economical bowlers, stands up against a youthful yet determined Pakistani side aiming to continue their impressive head-to-head record. There's also a bit of rain around but let's hope that doesn't affect the contest much. Stay tuned for the toss and team news.

The pitch at the Shere Bangla National Stadium is typically on the slower side, offering assistance to spinners as the game progresses. While pacers might find some early seam movement, batters who settle in can play their strokes freely.

However, Pakistan will pose a formidable challenge despite some notable absentees. While key players like Babar Azam and Mohammad Rizwan are missing, a young Pakistan side, led by Salman Agha, will be eager to assert their dominance. Historically, Pakistan holds a significant edge in T20I encounters, having won 19 out of 22 matches against Bangladesh, including a commanding 3-0 clean sweep in their most recent series a month ago in Lahore. The visitors will be looking to replicate that performance and maintain their winning rhythm away from home.

Hello and a warm welcome to one and all. The cricketing rivalry between Bangladesh and Pakistan rekindles as they lock horns in the 1st T20I of a three-match series at the Shere Bangla National Stadium in Mirpur. Bangladesh enters this contest with a morale boost, having recently secured a 2-1 T20I series victory over Sri Lanka on their home turf. With home advantage and a settled squad, captain Litton Das will be keen to build on that momentum and aim for a strong start in front of their fervent supporters.
... MATCH DAY ...

Cricket fans are in for a treat as the action-packed calendar continues to deliver thrilling contests across all formats. The spotlight now shifts to the subcontinent, where Bangladesh prepares to welcome Pakistan for what promises to be an electrifying three-match T20I series. This matchup brings together two passionate cricketing nations known for their intense rivalry and competitive spirit. The iconic Shere Bangla Stadium in Dhaka will serve as the battleground for all three encounters, providing a familiar home advantage for the hosts. Bangladesh arrives at this series with a spring in their step following their recent performances. While their comprehensive tour of Sri Lanka produced mixed results across formats, the home side found their rhythm when it mattered most, securing the T20I series with a convincing 2-1 victory. That positive finish has clearly influenced their approach, as the selectors have opted to maintain faith in the same squad that delivered success in Sri Lankan conditions. Litton Das has carved out a unique place in Bangladesh cricket history, becoming the first captain to secure two overseas T20I series victories - first conquering the West Indies last year and then triumphing in Sri Lanka recently. Yet sandwiched between these impressive achievements is a stark reminder of Pakistan's strength, as Das witnessed his side suffer a complete 3-0 whitewash against the very same Pakistani outfit during their tour to Lahore in May-June this year. One of the brightest features for them was their overall performance across both departments. The recent Sri Lankan tour showcased Bangladesh's batting depth, with several players stepping up when it mattered most. Tanzid Hasan emerged as a bright prospect in their batting, while Litton Das, Tawhid Hridoy, and Shamim Hossain all delivered crucial contributions with the bat, demonstrating the team's improved middle-order stability and opening partnerships. On the bowling front, the spin-pace combination proved highly effective. Mahedi Hasan emerged as the standout performer. The supporting cast of Rishad Hossain and veteran Mustafizur Rahman maintained remarkable consistency throughout the series, both finishing with impressive economy rates below six runs per over, showcasing the team's well-rounded bowling attack. With the lethal pace trio of Tanzim Hasan Sakib, Taskin Ahmed and Shoriful Islam also included in the side, they look primed to dominate at home this time around. Pakistan arrives with a squad that blends familiar faces with fresh talent, creating an intriguing mix rather than a complete overhaul. Under Mike Hesson's still-developing tenure as head coach, this represents just their second white-ball assignment together, adding layers of tactical evolution to their approach. Key absences have reshaped their bowling dynamics significantly. The injury-enforced unavailability of established names like Shadab Khan and Haris Rauf has opened doors for uncapped prospects Ahmed Daniyal and Salman Mirza to stake their claims in the pace department. This reshuffling leaves Abbas Afridi, with his modest tally of 21 T20Is, as their most seasoned fast bowler. Their batting framework showcases an appealing generational blend. The youthful energy of Sahibzada Farhan, Saim Ayub, and Mohammad Haris meshes with the seasoned expertise of captain Salman Agha and the explosive Fakhar Zaman. The squad's versatility gets amplified through the all-round contributions of Faheem Ashraf, Khushdil Shah, and Mohammad Nawaz, while Sufiyan Muqeem provides the spin variation. Bangladesh confronts a daunting historical reality in this matchup. Managing just three victories from 22 T20I encounters against Pakistan represents more than underwhelming results. Their home record tells an even starker story, with merely two wins from seven matches in Mirpur, making their supposed fortress feel a bit vulnerable against these opponents. Pakistan's recent away form presents its own challenges. Their overseas expeditions have produced inconsistent results recently, finding success only against Zimbabwe while stumbling against big oppositions like New Zealand, South Africa, and suffering a comprehensive whitewash in Australia. This away vulnerability presents Bangladesh with a genuine opportunity to capitalize. Both teams view this series through the lens of the 2026 T20 World Cup preparation in India, making every performance a crucial building block for future success. Also, it’s been absolutely pelting down in this part of the world due to monsoons at peak, and it will be crucial to see how it affects the strategies of the two sides. All in all, it’s shaping up to be another blockbuster series between these rivals.
